sanskrit: yathā prakāśayaty ekaḥ kṛtsnaṃ lokam imaṃ raviḥ kṣetraṃ kṣetrī tathā kṛtsnaṃ prakāśayati bhārata
english: As the single sun illumines this whole world, so does the Field-knower illumine the entire Field, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kṣetrakṣetrajñayor evam antaraṃ jñānacakṣuṣā bhūtaprakṛtimokṣaṃ ca ye vidur yānti te param
english: Those who thus discern, with the eye of knowledge, the difference between the Field and the Field-knower, and the release of beings from material nature—they attain the Supreme.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca paraṃ bhūyaḥ pravakṣyāmi jñānānāṃ jñānam uttamam yaj jñātvā munayaḥ sarve parāṃ siddhim ito gatāḥ
english: The Blessed Lord said: Once more I shall declare the supreme knowledge, the highest of all knowings, by knowing which all the sages have passed from here to the highest perfection.

sanskrit: idaṃ jñānam upāśritya mama sādharmyam āgatāḥ sarge 'pi nopajāyante pralaye na vyathanti ca
english: Having taken refuge in this knowledge and come to share in My own nature, they are not born again even at a new creation, nor are they disturbed at the dissolution.

sanskrit: mama yonir mahad brahma tasmin garbhaṃ dadhāmy aham saṃbhavaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tato bhavati bhārata
english: My womb is the great Brahman; in it I cast the seed. From that, O Bhārata, comes the birth of all beings.

sanskrit: sarvayoniṣu kaunteya mūrtayaḥ saṃbhavanti yāḥ tāsāṃ brahma mahad yonir ahaṃ bījapradaḥ pitā
english: Whatever forms take birth in all the wombs, O son of Kuntī, the great Brahman is their womb, and I am the seed-giving father.

sanskrit: sattvaṃ rajas tama iti guṇāḥ prakṛtisaṃbhavāḥ nibadhnanti mahābāho dehe dehinam avyayam
english: Goodness, passion, and darkness—these are the qualities born of material nature, O mighty-armed; they bind the imperishable embodied one within the body.

sanskrit: tatra sattvaṃ nirmalatvāt prakāśakam anāmayam sukhasaṅgena badhnāti jñānasaṅgena cānagha
english: Of these, goodness, being pure, is luminous and free from ill; it binds, O sinless one, through attachment to happiness and through attachment to knowledge.

sanskrit: rajo rāgātmakaṃ viddhi tṛṣṇāsaṅgasamudbhavam tan nibadhnāti kaunteya karmasaṅgena dehinam
english: Know passion to be of the nature of craving, arising from thirst and attachment; it binds the embodied one, O son of Kuntī, through attachment to action.

sanskrit: tamas tv ajñānajaṃ viddhi mohanaṃ sarvadehinām pramādālasyanidrābhis tan nibadhnāti bhārata
english: But darkness, know, is born of ignorance and deludes all embodied beings; it binds, O Bhārata, through heedlessness, sloth, and sleep.

sanskrit: sattvaṃ sukhe sañjayati rajaḥ karmaṇi bhārata jñānam āvṛtya tu tamaḥ pramāde sañjayaty uta
english: Goodness binds one to happiness, O Bhārata, and passion to action; but darkness, veiling knowledge, binds one to heedlessness.

sanskrit: rajas tamaś cābhibhūya sattvaṃ bhavati bhārata rajaḥ sattvaṃ tamaś caiva tamaḥ sattvaṃ rajas tathā
english: Goodness prevails by overpowering passion and darkness, O Bhārata; and passion overpowers goodness and darkness, while darkness overpowers goodness and passion.

sanskrit: sarvadvāreṣu dehe 'smin prakāśa upajāyate jñānaṃ yadā tadā vidyād vivṛddhaṃ sattvam ity uta
english: When through all the gates of this body the light of knowledge arises, then one should know that goodness has grown strong.

sanskrit: lobhaḥ pravṛttir ārambhaḥ karmaṇām aśamaḥ spṛhā rajasy etāni jāyante vivṛddhe bharatarṣabha
english: Greed, activity, the undertaking of works, restlessness, and longing—these arise when passion has grown strong, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: aprakāśo 'pravṛttiś ca pramādo moha eva ca tamasy etāni jāyante vivṛddhe kurunandana
english: Darkness, inertia, heedlessness, and delusion—these arise when darkness has grown strong, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: yadā sattve pravṛddhe tu pralayaṃ yāti dehabhṛt tadottamavidāṃ lokān amalān pratipadyate
english: When the embodied one meets dissolution while goodness is strong, he then attains the spotless worlds of those who know the highest.

sanskrit: rajasi pralayaṃ gatvā karmasaṅgiṣu jāyate tathā pralīnas tamasi mūḍhayoniṣu jāyate
english: Meeting dissolution in passion, one is born among those attached to action; and dissolving in darkness, one is born in the wombs of the deluded.

sanskrit: karmaṇaḥ sukṛtasyāhuḥ sāttvikaṃ nirmalaṃ phalam rajasas tu phalaṃ duḥkham ajñānaṃ tamasaḥ phalam
english: They say the fruit of good action is of the nature of goodness, pure; but the fruit of passion is suffering, and the fruit of darkness is ignorance.

sanskrit: sattvāt saṃjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca pramādamohau tamaso bhavato 'jñānam eva ca
english: From goodness arises knowledge, and from passion greed; from darkness arise heedlessness, delusion, and ignorance.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ gacchanti sattvasthā madhye tiṣṭhanti rājasāḥ jaghanyaguṇavṛttasthā adho gacchanti tāmasāḥ
english: Those established in goodness go upward; the passionate remain in the middle; and those who dwell in the workings of the lowest quality, the darkened, go downward.

sanskrit: nānyaṃ guṇebhyaḥ kartāraṃ yadā draṣṭānupaśyati guṇebhyaś ca paraṃ vetti madbhāvaṃ so 'dhigacchati
english: When the seer perceives no agent other than the qualities, and knows that which is beyond the qualities, he attains to My being.

sanskrit: guṇān etān atītya trīn dehī dehasamudbhavān janmamṛtyujarāduḥkhair vimukto 'mṛtam aśnute
english: Transcending these three qualities that spring from the body, the embodied one, freed from birth, death, old age, and sorrow, attains immortality.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca kair liṅgais trīn guṇān etān atīto bhavati prabho kimācāraḥ kathaṃ caitāṃs trīn guṇān ativartate
english: Arjuna said: By what marks is one known who has transcended these three qualities, O Lord? What is his conduct, and how does he pass beyond these three qualities?

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca prakāśaṃ ca pravṛttiṃ ca moham eva ca pāṇḍava na dveṣṭi saṃpravṛttāni na nivṛttāni kāṅkṣati
english: The Blessed Lord said: He who hates not illumination, activity, or delusion when they arise, O Pāṇḍava, nor longs for them when they cease;

sanskrit: udāsīnavad āsīno guṇair yo na vicālyate guṇā vartanta ity eva yo 'vatiṣṭhati neṅgate
english: who, seated as though indifferent, is not disturbed by the qualities; who, thinking only "the qualities are at work," stands firm and does not waver;

sanskrit: samaduḥkhasukhaḥ svasthaḥ samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ tulyapriyāpriyo dhīras tulyanindātmasaṃstutiḥ
english: who is alike in sorrow and joy, self-poised, regarding clod, stone, and gold as equal; who is steadfast, the same toward the dear and the unwelcome, the same in blame and in praise of himself;

sanskrit: mānāvamānayos tulyas tulyo mitrāripakṣayoḥ sarvārambhaparityāgī guṇātītaḥ sa ucyate
english: the same in honor and dishonor, the same toward the side of friend and of foe, renouncing all undertakings—he is said to have transcended the qualities.

sanskrit: māṃ ca yo 'vyabhicāreṇa bhaktiyogena sevate sa guṇān samatītyaitān brahmabhūyāya kalpate
english: And he who serves Me with unswerving devotion in yoga—he, transcending these qualities, is fit to become Brahman.

sanskrit: brahmaṇo hi pratiṣṭhāham amṛtasyāvyayasya ca śāśvatasya ca dharmasya sukhasyaikāntikasya ca
english: For I am the ground of Brahman, of the immortal and imperishable, of the eternal dharma, and of absolute bliss.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca ūrdhvamūlam adhaḥśākham aśvatthaṃ prāhur avyayam chandāṃsi yasya parṇāni yas taṃ veda sa vedavit
english: The Blessed Lord said: They speak of an imperishable aśvattha tree, with roots above and branches below, whose leaves are the hymns; he who knows it is a knower of the Vedas.

sanskrit: adhaś cordhvaṃ prasṛtās tasya śākhā; guṇapravṛddhā viṣayapravālāḥ adhaś ca mūlāny anusaṃtatāni; karmānubandhīni manuṣyaloke
english: Its branches stretch below and above, nourished by the qualities, with sense-objects as their twigs; and below, its roots reach onward, binding to action in the world of men.

sanskrit: na rūpam asyeha tathopalabhyate; nānto na cādir na ca saṃpratiṣṭhā aśvattham enaṃ suvirūḍhamūlam; asaṅgaśastreṇa dṛḍhena chittvā
english: Its form is not perceived here as it truly is—it has no end, no beginning, no foundation. Having cut down this aśvattha with its firmly grown roots, by the strong axe of detachment,

sanskrit: tataḥ padaṃ tatparimārgitavyaṃ; yasmin gatā na nivartanti bhūyaḥ tam eva cādyaṃ puruṣaṃ prapadye; yataḥ pravṛttiḥ prasṛtā purāṇī
english: then that goal is to be sought, gaining which one returns no more: "I take refuge in that primal Person from whom the ancient streaming-forth has flowed."

sanskrit: nirmānamohā jitasaṅgadoṣā; adhyātmanityā vinivṛttakāmāḥ dvaṃdvair vimuktāḥ sukhaduḥkhasaṃjñair; gacchanty amūḍhāḥ padam avyayaṃ tat
english: Free from pride and delusion, having conquered the fault of attachment, ever devoted to the supreme Self, with desires stilled, released from the dualities known as pleasure and pain—the undeluded go to that imperishable goal.

sanskrit: na tad bhāsayate sūryo na śaśāṅko na pāvakaḥ yad gatvā na nivartante tad dhāma paramaṃ mama
english: Neither sun nor moon nor fire illumines that, gaining which they return no more—that is My supreme abode.

sanskrit: mamaivāṃśo jīvaloke jīvabhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ manaḥṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi prakṛtisthāni karṣati
english: An eternal portion of My very Self, become a living soul in the world of the living, draws to itself the senses, with mind as the sixth, that abide in material nature.

sanskrit: śarīraṃ yad avāpnoti yac cāpy utkrāmatīśvaraḥ gṛhītvaitāni saṃyāti vāyur gandhān ivāśayāt
english: When the lord of the body takes on a body, and again when he departs from it, he takes these along and moves on, as the wind bears scents from their source.

sanskrit: śrotraṃ cakṣuḥ sparśanaṃ ca rasanaṃ ghrāṇam eva ca adhiṣṭhāya manaś cāyaṃ viṣayān upasevate
english: Presiding over hearing, sight, touch, taste, and smell, and over the mind as well, this one enjoys the objects of the senses.

sanskrit: utkrāmantaṃ sthitaṃ vāpi bhuñjānaṃ vā guṇānvitam vimūḍhā nānupaśyanti paśyanti jñānacakṣuṣaḥ
english: Whether departing, abiding, or enjoying, accompanied by the qualities, the deluded do not perceive him; but those with the eye of knowledge perceive him.

sanskrit: yatanto yoginaś cainaṃ paśyanty ātmany avasthitam yatanto 'py akṛtātmāno nainaṃ paśyanty acetasaḥ
english: The yogins, striving, behold him established in the self; but the unrefined of soul, the mindless, though they strive, do not behold him.

sanskrit: yad ādityagataṃ tejo jagad bhāsayate 'khilam yac candramasi yac cāgnau tat tejo viddhi māmakam
english: The radiance that resides in the sun and illumines the whole world, and that which is in the moon and in fire—know that radiance to be Mine.

sanskrit: gām āviśya ca bhūtāni dhārayāmy aham ojasā puṣṇāmi cauṣadhīḥ sarvāḥ somo bhūtvā rasātmakaḥ
english: Entering the earth, I sustain all beings by My energy; and becoming the sap-filled Soma, I nourish all the plants.

sanskrit: ahaṃ vaiśvānaro bhūtvā prāṇināṃ deham āśritaḥ prāṇāpānasamāyuktaḥ pacāmy annaṃ caturvidham
english: Becoming the fire Vaiśvānara, I dwell in the bodies of living creatures and, joined with the in-breath and out-breath, I digest the four kinds of food.

sanskrit: sarvasya cāhaṃ hṛdi saṃniviṣṭo; mattaḥ smṛtir jñānam apohanaṃ ca vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyo; vedāntakṛd vedavid eva cāham
english: And I am seated in the heart of all; from Me come memory, knowledge, and their loss. By all the Vedas I alone am to be known; I am the author of Vedānta and the knower of the Vedas.

sanskrit: dvāv imau puruṣau loke kṣaraś cākṣara eva ca kṣaraḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni kūṭastho 'kṣara ucyate
english: There are these two persons in the world, the perishable and the imperishable. The perishable is all beings; the unchanging is called the imperishable.

sanskrit: uttamaḥ puruṣas tv anyaḥ paramātmety udāhṛtaḥ yo lokatrayam āviśya bibharty avyaya īśvaraḥ
english: But the Supreme Person is another, declared to be the highest Self, who, entering the three worlds, sustains them—the imperishable Lord.

sanskrit: yasmāt kṣaram atīto 'ham akṣarād api cottamaḥ ato 'smi loke vede ca prathitaḥ puruṣottamaḥ
english: Since I transcend the perishable and am higher even than the imperishable, therefore in the world and in the Veda I am renowned as the Supreme Person.

sanskrit: yo mām evam asaṃmūḍho jānāti puruṣottamam sa sarvavid bhajati māṃ sarvabhāvena bhārata
english: He who, undeluded, knows Me thus as the Supreme Person—he, knowing all, worships Me with his whole being, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: iti guhyatamaṃ śāstram idam uktaṃ mayānagha etad buddhvā buddhimān syāt kṛtakṛtyaś ca bhārata
english: Thus this most secret teaching has been declared by Me, O sinless one. Awakening to this, a man becomes wise and has accomplished all there is to do, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca abhayaṃ sattvasaṃśuddhir jñānayogavyavasthitiḥ dānaṃ damaś ca yajñaś ca svādhyāyas tapa ārjavam
english: The Blessed Lord said: Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadfastness in the yoga of knowledge, charity, self-restraint, sacrifice, study of the scriptures, austerity, and uprightness;

sanskrit: ahiṃsā satyam akrodhas tyāgaḥ śāntir apaiśunam dayā bhūteṣv aloluptvaṃ mārdavaṃ hrīr acāpalam
english: non-violence, truth, freedom from anger, renunciation, peace, freedom from slander, compassion toward beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty, and steadiness;

sanskrit: tejaḥ kṣamā dhṛtiḥ śaucam adroho nātimānitā bhavanti saṃpadaṃ daivīm abhijātasya bhārata
english: vigor, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, freedom from malice, and freedom from overweening pride—these belong, O Bhārata, to one born to the divine endowment.

sanskrit: dambho darpo 'timānaś ca krodhaḥ pāruṣyam eva ca ajñānaṃ cābhijātasya pārtha saṃpadam āsurīm
english: Hypocrisy, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness, and ignorance—these belong, O Pārtha, to one born to the demonic endowment.

sanskrit: daivī saṃpad vimokṣāya nibandhāyāsurī matā mā śucaḥ saṃpadaṃ daivīm abhijāto 'si pāṇḍava
english: The divine endowment is held to lead to liberation, the demonic to bondage. Grieve not, O Pāṇḍava; you are born to the divine endowment.

sanskrit: dvau bhūtasargau loke 'smin daiva āsura eva ca daivo vistaraśaḥ prokta āsuraṃ pārtha me śṛṇu
english: There are two orders of created beings in this world, the divine and the demonic. The divine has been described at length; now hear from Me, O Pārtha, of the demonic.

sanskrit: pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca janā na vidur āsurāḥ na śaucaṃ nāpi cācāro na satyaṃ teṣu vidyate
english: Demonic men know neither action nor abstention from action; in them there is found neither purity nor good conduct nor truth.

sanskrit: asatyam apratiṣṭhaṃ te jagad āhur anīśvaram aparasparasaṃbhūtaṃ kim anyat kāmahaitukam
english: They say the world is without truth, without foundation, without a Lord, brought into being by no orderly mutual cause—what else but born of desire?

sanskrit: etāṃ dṛṣṭim avaṣṭabhya naṣṭātmāno 'lpabuddhayaḥ prabhavanty ugrakarmāṇaḥ kṣayāya jagato 'hitāḥ
english: Holding fast to this view, ruined in soul and feeble in understanding, they rise up as enemies of the world, doers of fierce deeds, bent on its destruction.

sanskrit: kāmam āśritya duṣpūraṃ dambhamānamadānvitāḥ mohād gṛhītvāsadgrāhān pravartante 'śucivratāḥ
english: Clinging to insatiable desire, filled with hypocrisy, conceit, and pride, having seized through delusion upon false notions, they act with impure resolves.

sanskrit: cintām aparimeyāṃ ca pralayāntām upāśritāḥ kāmopabhogaparamā etāvad iti niścitāḥ
english: Beset by measureless cares that end only with death, devoted to the enjoyment of desires as the highest aim, convinced that this is all there is;

sanskrit: āśāpāśaśatair baddhāḥ kāmakrodhaparāyaṇāḥ īhante kāmabhogārtham anyāyenārthasaṃcayān
english: bound by a hundred cords of hope, given over to desire and anger, they strive to amass wealth by unjust means for the sake of sensual enjoyment.

sanskrit: idam adya mayā labdham idaṃ prāpsye manoratham idam astīdam api me bhaviṣyati punar dhanam
english: "This I have gained today; this longing of my heart I shall attain; this is mine, and this wealth too shall be mine hereafter."

sanskrit: asau mayā hataḥ śatrur haniṣye cāparān api īśvaro 'ham ahaṃ bhogī siddho 'haṃ balavān sukhī
english: "That foe I have slain, and others too I shall slay. I am the lord, I am the enjoyer, I am successful, mighty, and happy."

sanskrit: āḍhyo 'bhijanavān asmi ko 'nyo 'sti sadṛśo mayā yakṣye dāsyāmi modiṣya ity ajñānavimohitāḥ
english: "I am rich and high-born; who else is equal to me? I shall sacrifice, I shall give, I shall rejoice"—thus deluded by ignorance,

sanskrit: anekacittavibhrāntā mohajālasamāvṛtāḥ prasaktāḥ kāmabhogeṣu patanti narake 'śucau
english: bewildered by many thoughts, enmeshed in the net of delusion, addicted to the enjoyment of desires, they fall into a foul hell.

sanskrit: ātmasaṃbhāvitāḥ stabdhā dhanamānamadānvitāḥ yajante nāmayajñais te dambhenāvidhipūrvakam
english: Self-conceited, unbending, filled with the pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform sacrifices that are sacrifices in name only, with hypocrisy and without due rite.

sanskrit: ahaṃkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca saṃśritāḥ mām ātmaparadeheṣu pradviṣanto 'bhyasūyakāḥ
english: Given over to egotism, force, arrogance, desire, and anger, these spiteful men hate Me, who dwell within their own bodies and the bodies of others.

sanskrit: tān ahaṃ dviṣataḥ krūrān saṃsāreṣu narādhamān kṣipāmy ajasram aśubhān āsurīṣv eva yoniṣu
english: These haters, cruel and vile among men, the most degraded, I hurl ceaselessly, those evil ones, into demonic wombs amid the rounds of rebirth.

sanskrit: āsurīṃ yonim āpannā mūḍhā janmani janmani mām aprāpyaiva kaunteya tato yānty adhamāṃ gatim
english: Fallen into demonic wombs, deluded birth after birth, never reaching Me, O son of Kuntī, they thence go to the lowest course.

sanskrit: trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanam ātmanaḥ kāmaḥ krodhas tathā lobhas tasmād etat trayaṃ tyajet
english: Threefold is this gate of hell, the ruin of the self—desire, anger, and greed; therefore one should abandon these three.

sanskrit: etair vimuktaḥ kaunteya tamodvārais tribhir naraḥ ācaraty ātmanaḥ śreyas tato yāti parāṃ gatim
english: Released from these three gates of darkness, O son of Kuntī, a man works for the good of his soul and thence goes to the supreme course.

sanskrit: yaḥ śāstravidhim utsṛjya vartate kāmakārataḥ na sa siddhim avāpnoti na sukhaṃ na parāṃ gatim
english: He who, casting aside the ordinance of scripture, acts under the impulse of desire attains neither perfection nor happiness nor the supreme course.

sanskrit: tasmāc chāstraṃ pramāṇaṃ te kāryākāryavyavasthitau jñātvā śāstravidhānoktaṃ karma kartum ihārhasi
english: Therefore let scripture be your authority in determining what is to be done and what is not; knowing what is declared by the ordinance of scripture, you should act here in this world.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca ye śāstravidhim utsṛjya yajante śraddhayānvitāḥ teṣāṃ niṣṭhā tu kā kṛṣṇa sattvam āho rajas tamaḥ
english: Arjuna said: Those who, casting aside the ordinance of scripture, yet sacrifice filled with faith—what is their standing, O Kṛṣṇa? Is it goodness, passion, or darkness?

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca trividhā bhavati śraddhā dehināṃ sā svabhāvajā sāttvikī rājasī caiva tāmasī ceti tāṃ śṛṇu
english: The Blessed Lord said: The faith of embodied beings is of three kinds, born of their own nature—of goodness, of passion, and of darkness. Hear of it.

sanskrit: sattvānurūpā sarvasya śraddhā bhavati bhārata śraddhāmayo 'yaṃ puruṣo yo yacchraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ
english: The faith of each is in accord with his nature, O Bhārata. Man is made of his faith; as his faith is, so is he.

sanskrit: yajante sāttvikā devān yakṣarakṣāṃsi rājasāḥ pretān bhūtagaṇāṃś cānye yajante tāmasā janāḥ
english: Those of goodness worship the gods; those of passion worship the yakṣas and rākṣasas; and the others, men of darkness, worship the departed and the hordes of spirits.

sanskrit: aśāstravihitaṃ ghoraṃ tapyante ye tapo janāḥ dambhāhaṃkārasaṃyuktāḥ kāmarāgabalānvitāḥ
english: Those men who practice grim austerity not ordained by scripture, joined to hypocrisy and egotism, driven by the force of desire and passion,

sanskrit: karśayantaḥ śarīrasthaṃ bhūtagrāmam acetasaḥ māṃ caivāntaḥśarīrasthaṃ tān viddhy āsuraniścayān
english: torturing, in their senselessness, the host of elements within the body, and Me too who dwell within the body—know them to be of demonic resolve.

sanskrit: āhāras tv api sarvasya trividho bhavati priyaḥ yajñas tapas tathā dānaṃ teṣāṃ bhedam imaṃ śṛṇu
english: The food, too, that is dear to each is of three kinds, and so are sacrifice, austerity, and giving. Hear now of their distinction.
